## Purpose and entry points
CISO Assistant is an API-first cybersecurity GRC platform: it manages reusable controls, compliance assessments, risks, evidence, remediation, third parties, privacy, and reporting. The primary server entry points are the Django project at `backend/manage.py`, `backend/ciso_assistant/urls.py`, and ASGI/WSGI modules in `backend/ciso_assistant/asgi.py` and `backend/ciso_assistant/wsgi.py`. The user-facing application is a SvelteKit frontend rooted at `frontend/src/routes/+layout.svelte`, with the authenticated app under `frontend/src/routes/(app)`.

## Delivery topology and runtimes
The core runtime is Python/Django behind Gunicorn, plus a Node/SvelteKit SSR frontend. Huey executes asynchronous/background tasks, including notifications, integrations, and domain work. Docker Compose is the standard local/self-hosted deployment path (`docker-compose.yml`, `backend/startup.sh`); generated deployment variants live in `config/templates`. Kubernetes is supported through Helm (`charts/ciso-assistant-next/templates/backend/deployment.yaml`, `charts/ciso-assistant-next/templates/frontend/deployment.yaml`). Caddy is the default reverse-proxy/TLS boundary (`Caddyfile`, `frontend/Caddyfile`).

Persistent data uses SQLite by default or PostgreSQL in production; attachments can remain filesystem-backed or use S3-compatible/AWS S3 or Azure Blob storage. The database schema is Django-model/migration driven.

## Core GRC domain and API boundary
`backend/core/models.py` is the central domain model for assets, perimeters, controls, evidence, assessments, risks, findings, incidents, tasks, and related shared concepts. `backend/core/views.py`, `backend/core/serializers.py`, and `backend/core/urls.py` expose the main REST surface. The frontend’s generic model routes proxy/render these resources through `frontend/src/routes/(app)/(internal)/[model=urlmodel]`.

A defining design principle is separation of reusable control implementation from framework-specific compliance assessment. Assessment results, applied controls, evidence, risk scenarios, and action plans can therefore be related across scopes rather than duplicated. Mapping logic is a dedicated cross-framework boundary in `backend/core/mappings/engine.py` and `backend/core/mappings/merge.py`.

## Libraries, frameworks, and assessment lifecycle
Versioned YAML libraries provide frameworks, control catalogs, threat catalogs, mappings, risk matrices, presets, quick forms, and workflow templates under `backend/library/libraries`. The library subsystem parses/builds/stores these artifacts and exposes import/load operations through `backend/library/builder.py`, `backend/library/models.py`, and `backend/library/views.py`.

Libraries instantiate framework structures used by compliance assessments; assessments collect requirement-level answers/evidence, calculate scores, derive mappings and remediation, then export reports. The interactive framework builder is implemented in `frontend/src/lib/components/FrameworkBuilder/FrameworkBuilder.svelte`; library authoring/import is available through `frontend/src/routes/(app)/(internal)/experimental/library-builder`.

## Identity, tenancy/scoping, and portals
IAM is an architectural gate before domain access: users, roles, assignments, folders, service accounts, SSO, MFA, and SCIM are implemented in `backend/iam/models.py`, `backend/iam/authentication.py`, and `backend/iam/scim/views.py`. Folder/domain scope and permission checks constrain API queries and UI context. Authentication supports local accounts plus OIDC/SAML (`backend/iam/sso/oidc/views.py`, `backend/iam/sso/saml/views.py`).

The frontend separates internal users from constrained third-party/auditee experiences in `frontend/src/routes/(app)/(third-party)`. Public trust/portal publication is a separate exposure boundary via `backend/portals/views.py` and `frontend/src/routes/trust`.

## Automation, events, and integrations
The workflow engine models executable graphs with triggers, actions, scheduling, authorization, validation, and run state in `backend/automation/workflows/engine.py`, `backend/automation/workflows/graph.py`, and `backend/automation/workflows/triggers.py`. Its visual editor is `frontend/src/routes/(app)/(internal)/workflows/[id=uuid]/WorkflowCanvas.svelte`. Shipped workflow-library YAML can instantiate operational automations.

External boundaries include Jira and ServiceNow synchronization (`backend/integrations/itsm/jira/integration.py`, `backend/integrations/itsm/servicenow/integration.py`), outbound webhooks (`backend/webhooks/service.py`), and Kafka command ingestion through the standalone dispatcher (`dispatcher/dispatcher.py`, `dispatcher/utils/kafka.py`). The Python CLI/MCP server provides programmatic and agent-facing API access (`cli/clica.py`, `cli/ca_mcp/server.py`). n8n and Power BI connectors are maintained integration packages under `automation/n8n/n8n-nodes-ca` and `automation/powerbi/connector`.

## Specialized intelligence and domain modules
Risk extends from qualitative assessments in core to EBIOS RM (`backend/ebios_rm/models.py`), quantitative cyber risk (`backend/crq/models.py`), resilience/BIA and DORA reporting (`backend/resilience/models.py`), and third-party risk (`backend/tprm/models.py`). Privacy processing/register functionality is isolated in `backend/privacy/models.py`.

AI/chat is a bounded subsystem: provider abstraction, scoped RAG, embeddings, knowledge graph, tool calls, and background indexing reside in `backend/chat/providers.py`, `backend/chat/rag.py`, and `backend/chat/knowledge_graph.py`; it can use external/local AI providers and Qdrant indexing. Security-intelligence feeds enrich advisory/vulnerability data through `backend/sec_intel/feeds.py`.
